title: Oister Global Launches ₹600 Cr Growth-Stage Focused Deeptech Fund
summary: Oister Global launches 600 crore rupee growth-stage deeptech venture fund
detailed: Oister Global has launched the Oister Deep Tech Fund with a target corpus of ₹400 crore and a ₹200 crore greenshoe option, totaling a potential ₹600 crore ($72M+).
The fund will back 8 to 10 mature, revenue-generating Indian deeptech startups across sectors like space, defense, semiconductors, and quantum technology.
Involved organizations include asset manager Oister Global and SEBI (registered as a Category II AIF).

This matters because it provides dedicated growth-stage capital to bridge the funding gap for startups that have moved past early-stage R&D and require patient capital for production scaling and commercialization.
sentences: The firm will target backing Indian startups developing technologies across strategic sectors.
The Oister Deep Tech Fund, registered as a SEBI Category II AIF, intends to raise ₹400 Cr, along with a ₹200 Cr greenshoe option to build a concentrated portfolio of 8-10 companies.
In a statement, the investment firm shared that it will focus on mature deeptech companies that have developed commercially viable technologies and are looking to scale their operations.
Its investment focus will span sectors like spacetech, defence and aerospace, semiconductors and electronics, quantum technologies, advanced mobility, advanced materials and energy storage.

The fund will target companies with proprietary intellectual property (IP), including patents in India and international markets, multiple revenue streams and customers across domestic and global markets.
“Early-stage investors back the idea, and larger institutions tend to wait until a company is well past its hardest years.
The growth stage in between, where technology turns into a business, has had very few committed investors.
That is the gap we saw, and it is why we launched the Oister Deep Tech Fund,” said Rohit Bhayana, cofounder and co-CEO of Oister Global.
The fund launch comes amid a growing investor interest in India’s budding deeptech ecosystem.
Recent examples include AUM Ventures’ ₹750 Cr India Innovation Fund II, Speciale Invest’s proposed ₹1,400 Cr growth-stage fund and Celesta Capital’s planned ₹2,000 Cr India-focused deeptech fund.
Meanwhile, Yali Capital closed its maiden deeptech fund at ₹893 Cr in July 2025.
As a result, the overall investment numbers have also been on the up.

Indian deeptech startups raised nearly $365 Mn across 66 deals in H1 2026, representing a 17% YoY growth in funding, compared with $310 Mn in H1 2025, according to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report: H1 2026.

Pertinent to note that much of this capital deployment has continued to remain concentrated in the early stage, with not many investors showing the same enthusiasm when it comes to startups operating in the latter stages.

Citing this discrepancy, Oister Global said that growth-stage funding can help bridge the gap by providing patient capital to companies that have already de-risked their technology but require larger investments to manufacture products, fulfil orders and expand into international markets.
The fund has already identified an initial shortlist of companies across its target sectors, with further investments to be evaluated as capital is deployed.
Oister previously backed startups in the country through its growth-stage and secondary investment vehicles.
Its portfolio includes companies such as BlackBuck, Servify, M1xchange, Kuku FM and Purplle, among others.
In May, it launched its third ACE fund with a ₹500 Cr corpus after the second ACE fund closed with a ₹400 Cr corpus, twice its initial target of ₹200 Cr.
The third fund took its total secondaries allotment to ₹1,000 Cr.
Besides directly investing in startups, Oister also operates with a fund of funds thesis.
Till date, it has turned limited partner for various startup funds for VC firms including Blume Ventures, Speciale Invest and Stride Ventures.
